title: Momentum Module 4 Lesson 1: Two Case Collisions custom practice

evidence_basis.originality_note: All prompts, numerical values and physical configurations are original; mapped Cambridge past-paper evidence informs cognitive demand and assessment structure only.

parts.prompt: Particle $P$ of mass $0.3\text{ kg}$ is moving with speed $5\text{ m s}^{-1}$ along a smooth horizontal plane when it collides directly with a stationary particle $Q$ of mass $0.6\text{ kg}$. After the collision, the speed of $P$ is $1\text{ m s}^{-1}$. Find the two possible speeds of $Q$ after the collision.

Particles $A$ and $B$, of masses $0.4\text{ kg}$ and $0.5\text{ kg}$ respectively, move towards each other on a smooth horizontal plane with speeds $6\text{ m s}^{-1}$ and $2\text{ m s}^{-1}$ respectively. After the collision, $A$ moves with speed $1.5\text{ m s}^{-1}$ in its original direction. Find the speed and direction of motion of $B$ after the collision.

Particle $A$ of mass $m\text{ kg}$ moves with speed $4\text{ m s}^{-1}$ along a smooth horizontal track and collides directly with a stationary particle $B$ of mass $0.5\text{ kg}$. In the collision, particle $B$ moves with speed $3\text{ m s}^{-1}$ and particle $A$ moves with speed $1\text{ m s}^{-1}$. Find the two possible values of $m$.

Particle $P$ of mass $0.2\text{ kg}$ moves with speed $6\text{ m s}^{-1}$ towards a stationary particle $Q$ of mass $0.4\text{ kg}$ on a smooth surface. After the collision, both particles have equal speeds $v\text{ m s}^{-1}$. Find the two possible values of $v$.

Particle $A$ of mass $0.5\text{ kg}$ travelling at $4\text{ m s}^{-1}$ collides directly with particle $B$ of mass $0.5\text{ kg}$ travelling in the same direction at $2\text{ m s}^{-1}$. Immediately after the collision, $A$ moves with speed $1\text{ m s}^{-1}$ in its original direction. Find the speed of $B$ after the collision.

Particle $X$ of mass $0.25\text{ kg}$ moves with speed $8\text{ m s}^{-1}$ along a straight horizontal track. It collides with another particle and leaves the collision with speed $2\text{ m s}^{-1}$. Calculate the two possible magnitudes of the impulse exerted on $X$.

questions.prompt: Particles $P$ of mass $0.3\text{ kg}$ and $Q$ of mass $0.5\text{ kg}$ move directly towards each other on a smooth horizontal plane with speeds $4\text{ m s}^{-1}$ and $2\text{ m s}^{-1}$ respectively. After $P$ and $Q$ collide, the speed of $P$ is $1\text{ m s}^{-1}$.

parts.label: (a)
parts.prompt: Find the two possible speeds of $Q$ after the collision.

parts.label: (b)
parts.prompt: For the case where $P$ rebounds in the opposite direction with speed $1\text{ m s}^{-1}$, calculate the loss in kinetic energy of the system caused by the collision.

questions.prompt: Particle $A$ of mass $0.2\text{ kg}$ is projected with speed $6\text{ m s}^{-1}$ on a smooth horizontal floor directly towards a stationary particle $B$ of mass $0.4\text{ kg}$. In the collision, the speed of $B$ is twice the speed of $A$.

parts.label: (a)
parts.prompt: Find the two possible values of the speed of $A$ after the collision.

parts.label: (b)
parts.prompt: Find the magnitude of the impulse exerted by $A$ on $B$ in each of the two cases.

questions.prompt: Particle $P$ of mass $m\text{ kg}$ is moving with speed $6\text{ m s}^{-1}$ on a smooth horizontal floor when it collides directly with a stationary particle $Q$ of mass $0.5\text{ kg}$. Immediately after the collision, $Q$ moves with speed $4\text{ m s}^{-1}$, and the speed of $P$ is $2\text{ m s}^{-1}$.

parts.label: (a)
parts.prompt: Find the two possible values of $m$.

parts.label: (b)
parts.prompt: Calculate the loss of kinetic energy of the system in each of the two cases, and state which case corresponds to a completely elastic collision.

questions.prompt: Particle $A$ of mass $0.6\text{ kg}$ travels with speed $4\text{ m s}^{-1}$ along a smooth horizontal section of a track and collides directly with a stationary particle $B$ of mass $0.3\text{ kg}$. Immediately after the collision, particle $A$ has speed $1\text{ m s}^{-1}$. Particle $B$ moves onto a rough horizontal section of the floor where the coefficient of friction is $\mu = 0.25$. Take $g = 10\text{ m s}^{-2}$.

parts.label: (a)
parts.prompt: Find the two possible speeds of $B$ immediately after the collision.

parts.label: (b)
parts.prompt: Find the deceleration of $B$ on the rough floor, and calculate the two possible distances $B$ slides before coming to rest.

questions.prompt: A particle $P$ of mass $0.5\text{ kg}$ is projected along a smooth horizontal track with speed $8\text{ m s}^{-1}$ and collides directly with a stationary particle $Q$ of mass $1.0\text{ kg}$ at the base of a smooth curved incline. Immediately after the collision, $P$ has speed $2\text{ m s}^{-1}$. Take $g = 10\text{ m s}^{-2}$.

parts.label: (a)
parts.prompt: Find the two possible speeds of $Q$ immediately after the collision.

parts.label: (b)
parts.prompt: Particle $Q$ moves off along the smooth curved incline and ascends to a maximum height $h$ above the horizontal track before coming to instantaneous rest. Calculate the two possible values of $h$.

questions.prompt: Three particles $A$, $B$, and $C$ lie in a straight line on a smooth horizontal table, with masses $0.4\text{ kg}$, $0.5\text{ kg}$, and $0.3\text{ kg}$ respectively. Initially, $B$ and $C$ are at rest. Particle $A$ is projected directly towards $B$ with speed $6\text{ m s}^{-1}$. After the collision between $A$ and $B$, the speed of $A$ is $1.5\text{ m s}^{-1}$.

parts.label: (a)
parts.prompt: Find the two possible speeds of $B$ immediately after the first collision.

parts.label: (b)
parts.prompt: Particle $B$ subsequently collides directly with stationary particle $C$ and coalesces with it. Find the speed of the combined particle $BC$ in each of the two cases.

parts.label: (c)
parts.prompt: For Case 1, where particle $A$ continues to move in its original direction with speed $1.5\text{ m s}^{-1}$, determine whether particle $A$ will ever collide with the combined particle $BC$.

questions.prompt: Particle $P$ of mass $m\text{ kg}$ is projected with speed $u\text{ m s}^{-1}$ along a smooth horizontal surface towards a stationary particle $Q$ of mass $0.6\text{ kg}$. In the direct collision between $P$ and $Q$, the speed of $Q$ after the collision is twice the speed of $P$ after the collision.

parts.label: (a)
parts.prompt: Show that the two possible expressions for the speed $V$ of particle $P$ after the collision in terms of $u$ and $m$ are $V = \frac{mu}{m + 1.2}$ and $V = \frac{mu}{1.2 - m}$ (for $m < 1.2$).

parts.label: (b)
parts.prompt: Given that $m = 0.4\text{ kg}$, find the numerical value of the ratio $\frac{V}{u}$ in both cases, and calculate the percentage of the original kinetic energy lost in Case 1.
